subject: tech
title: Taking Care of Devices
about: Looking after a tablet or computer: clean dry hands, no food or drinks nearby, two hands to carry it, a case, charging, gentle taps, eye breaks, a kind headphone volume, asking before downloads or purchases, what to try when it freezes, and naming simple problems (no sound, black screen, no internet) so a grown-up can fix them. NC K2-CS-04 (describe basic hardware and software problems) and K2-IC-04 (responsible logoff). Read it together: the tablet reads every question and choice aloud.
tip: When something goes wrong on the tablet, ask him to say what is wrong in words before you fix it: no sound, black screen or no internet.

cards.q: Your hands are sticky from a snack. What do you do before you touch the tablet?
cards.note: Clean, dry hands keep the screen clear and working. Sticky fingers leave smudges that are hard to clean off.

cards.q: Where should your juice go while you use the tablet?
cards.note: One spill can break a tablet for good. Drinks and snacks stay far away from it.

cards.q: How do you carry a tablet from one room to another?
cards.note: Two hands and a slow walk. A dropped tablet can crack.

cards.q: You want to watch a video. What do you do before you press play?
cards.note: Walking while looking at a screen means you cannot see steps, doors or toys on the floor. Sit first.

cards.q: What is the soft or hard cover around a tablet for?
cards.note: A case is like a helmet for the tablet. It softens bumps and drops.

cards.q: The battery picture is red and almost empty. What does the tablet need?
cards.note: Ask a grown-up to plug in the charger, then let the tablet fill up.

cards.q: How do you touch the screen when you tap a button?
cards.note: The screen feels even a soft tap. Hard pokes can crack it.

cards.q: You have looked at the screen for a long time. What is a good break for your eyes?
cards.note: Look out a window at something far away for a little while. Your eyes get to rest.

cards.q: A game says, get this new app! What do you do first?
cards.note: Some apps cost money or are not for kids. A grown-up checks first.

cards.q: A game asks you to buy more coins with real money. Who decides?
cards.note: Buying in a game uses real money. Always ask first. It is okay to say no to the game.

cards.q: You put on headphones. How loud should the sound be?
wrong: loud enough for the whole house
cards.note: If someone next to you can hear your headphones, it is too loud. Loud sound can hurt your ears.

cards.q: The game is frozen and stuck on the screen. What is a good first thing to try?
cards.note: Closing the app and opening it again fixes many stuck screens. If that does not work, a grown-up can help.

cards.q: You closed the app, but the tablet is still stuck. Who can help restart it?
cards.note: Restarting means turning it all the way off and on again. Many problems go away after a restart.

cards.q: The video plays but you hear nothing. What should you check first?
cards.note: Saying what is wrong helps fix it. No sound? Check the volume buttons and the mute switch.

cards.q: You press the button and the screen stays black. What is probably the problem?
cards.note: A black screen often means the battery is empty. Plug it in and wait a few minutes.

cards.q: The drawing app works, but websites will not open. What is probably off?
cards.note: No internet? Look for the Wi-Fi picture at the top of the screen. A grown-up can turn it back on.

cards.q: You are done with the tablet. What do you do before you put it away?
cards.note: Locking or logging out keeps your things safe until next time. Then put it back in its spot.
